clauses.reason: The operative clause states that the President does "do order that the said code of fair competition be and it is hereby approved". That is a section 3(a) approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Motor Vehicle Retailing Trade with no stated period, condition or exception, and it has legal effect only through that approval: under section 3(b) the code's provisions became the standards of fair competition for the trade, and under sections 3(c) and 3(f) violations were restrainable in equity and punishable as misdemeanors. Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, provides: "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed". The resolution states no other effective date, so the command ended as a prospective operative command on June 14, 1935. No earlier end is shown (see earlier_end_check). The June 16, 1935 expiry is not an end because section 1 of the resolution replaced it with April 1, 1936. Schechter (295 U.S. 495, decided May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization, not an end date.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 6321 (October 3, 1933) approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Motor Vehicle Retailing Trade under section 3(a) of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act. Read in full from the held American Presidency Project transcription (APP node 362146), registered as grade mirror_transcription (not an original). Identity and page check: the page record is a Common Crawl capture of 2025-09-06T08:31:47Z whose heading names Executive Order 6321, whose date (October 3, 1933) and subject agree with the text, and whose text sha256 equals the held text's. The census register and the WPA 1944 list (1933 Oct 3, p.542, approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Motor Vehicle Retailing Trade) give the same date and subject. The reviewed shared analysis (SHARED_ANALYSIS.md and review-shared/ADJUDICATION.json) applies: a code-dependent command that did not end earlier ended on June 14, 1935 by statutory repeal (S.J. Res. 113 sec. 2); Schechter (May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization, not an end date. No inventory correction was needed: the one machine clause is the operative paragraph, and the opening paragraph only recites the application, hearings and findings.

savings.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the approved code before June 14, 1935 are accrued consequences, and the section 5 exemption from the antitrust laws for action complying with an approved code taken while Title I was in effect is likewise an accrued effect for completed action. The proviso to section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 names agreements and action under them, not codes, and states no time limit; the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the section 5 exemption for past action under codes, and whatever exemption survives for past action is an accrued effect, not continued operation of this approval. Nothing in the held sources continues the approval after June 14, 1935.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1935-05-27: date the section 3 delegation was declared unconstitutional; validity characterization (void from issuance under then-prevailing doctrine), not an end date
source_notes.reason: A. L. A. Schechter Poultry Corp. v. United States, 295 U.S. 495, decided May 27, 1935: the Court held the section 3 code-making delegation unconstitutional and the Live Poultry Code provisions in question invalid. Recorded as a validity characterization for every section 3 code approval, not as this order's end; the judgment did not cancel or withdraw this order.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1933-06-16: enactment date of NIRA section 3; the provisions described were repealed on June 14, 1935 (S.J. Res. 113 sec. 2).
source_notes.reason: NIRA section 3 (48 Stat. 195, June 16, 1933): under 3(a) the President approved codes and could impose conditions of approval; under 3(b), 3(c) and 3(f) an approved code's provisions became standards of fair competition enforceable by injunction and as misdemeanors. These are the legal effects that section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 repealed.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1933-06-16: enactment date of NIRA section 5; S.J. Res. 113 (June 14, 1935) limited the exemption by proviso; the held text does not settle the proviso's effect on past action.
source_notes.reason: NIRA section 5 exempted from the antitrust laws any code approved and in effect under Title I and any complying action while Title I was in effect and for sixty days thereafter; any exemption for action taken before the repeal is an accrued effect, not continued operation of the approval.
